05. 1.
The learned Legal Aid Counsel being present virtual Court, High Court of Orissa, Sundargarh addresses arguments.

2. Under Section 439 of Cr.P.C., the BLAPL has been filed by the petitioner, now in jail custody in connection with Rajgangpur PS Case No.303 of 2022 corresponding to Special G.R. Case No.130 of 2022 pending on the file of learned Additional District Judge-cum-Presiding Officer, Special Court under POCSO Act, Sundargarh for alleged commission of offences under Sections 376(3) of IPC read with Section 4 of POCSO Act.

3. The matter has been listed before this Bench in terms of Standing Order No.2 dated 21.05.2023 as by earlier order dated 28.11.2023 passed in BLAPL No.7866 of 2023 filed by the present petitioner was dismissed by this Bench.
4. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner is in custody since more than 2 years and trial has not progressed and the petitioner seeks indulgence for grant of bail.

5. Pursuant to the direction of this Court by order dated 20th September, 2024 the informant has been informed and the learned counsel, Miss. Prusty appears and addresses arguments on behalf of the informant.

6. Learned counsel for the petitioner reiterates his submissions regarding grant of bail to the petitioner stating that the petitioner is in custody since 10.07.2022 and he may be shown indulgence as far as prayer for bail is concerned.

7. Learned Additional Government Advocate referring to the materials on record and the earlier order passed by this Bench dated 14.11.2023 disposed of on 28.11.2023 in BLAPL No.7866 of 2023 opposes the prayer for bail.

8. Learned Legal Aid Defence Counsel appearing on behalf of informant opposes the prayer for bail referring to the materials on record, earlier orders dated 28.11.2023 and 14.11.2023 passed by this Court and also referring to the apprehension of informant/victim.

9. Pursuant to the order passed by this Court on 23.12.2024, the learned Additional District Judge-cum- Presiding Officer, Special Court (POCSO), Sundargarh has provided instructions to the effect that out of 24 witnesses mentioned in the charge-sheet, 8 numbers of witnesses have been examined on behalf of the prosecution.
The next date of posting of the matter is 27th January, 2025 and approximately three months further time would be necessary for completion of the trial.

10. Having heard learned counsel for the petitioner, learned Additional Government Advocate for the State, learned counsel appearing on behalf of the informant and considering the materials on record, the earlier orders dated 14.11.2023 and 28.11.2023 passed in BLAPL no.7866 of 2023 this Court is not inclined to grant bail to the petitioner.
The prayer for bail stands rejected at this stage.
11. It is directed that the learned court in seisin of the matter shall do well to complete the trial, as expeditiously as possible, preferably by 30th April, 2025.
It is further directed that the prosecution as well as defence shall co-operate in conduct and completion of the trial expeditiously.
The order shall be communicated to the learned court in seisin of the matter.
